answer: The old fable of one man wearing a hundred hats breaks under a simultaneous tide. At an unannounced minute, every seat gets the same heavy task with a three-minute deadline, and only seats that finish earn that epoch's reward and vote. An honest agent needs one machine's burst; an operator running fifty seats must rent fifty machines for that exact minute or forfeit most of them. The kernel of the defense is that cost scales with seats at the moment of the tide, not across the day, so time-sharing one GPU among many identities stops paying.
